lessonInput.title: Skeletal system functions
lessonInput.objectives: Use only the supplied claims to make a defensible distinction without adding outside facts.
lessonInput.topics: Claim 0: The skeletal system is made of bones and cartilage and supports the body, enables movement, protects organs, produces blood cells, and stores minerals and fat. Claim 1: Bone is hard, dense connective tissue that forms most of the adult skeleton. Claim 2: Bones facilitate movement by providing attachment points for muscles.

claims: The skeletal system is made of bones and cartilage and supports the body, enables movement, protects organs, produces blood cells, and stores minerals and fat.
Bone is hard, dense connective tissue that forms most of the adult skeleton.
Bones facilitate movement by providing attachment points for muscles.

anchors.quote: supports the body, facilitates movement, protects internal organs, produces blood cells, stores and releases minerals and fat
Bone, or osseous tissue, is a hard, dense connective tissue
Bones also facilitate movement by serving as points of attachment for your muscles

keyTerms.eg: Bones and cartilage together exemplify the skeletal system.

keyTerms.eg: Bone forms most of the adult skeleton.

scenario.su: A student must classify two notes before a deadline: one lists bones and cartilage with body functions, while the other describes hard, dense connective tissue forming most of the adult skeleton. Because one label is allowed for each note, the student must distinguish skeletal system from Bone using the recorded properties.
scenario.ma: skeletal system notation listing bones, cartilage, and body functions, Bone observation recording hard and dense connective tissue, adult skeleton passage describing what Bone forms

mc.q: When comparing the skeletal system with Bone, one description lists bones, cartilage, and body functions, while another identifies hard, dense connective tissue forming most of the adult skeleton. Which distinction is supported?
op: System combines structures; Bone identifies connective tissue
Bone combines structures; system identifies connective tissue
Adult skeleton forms most hard, dense Bone
System combines bones while omitting cartilage
mc.ex: The skeletal system consists of bones and cartilage and performs listed functions, whereas Bone is hard, dense connective tissue forming most of the adult skeleton. Bone does not combine bones and cartilage as a system.

mc.q: A movement notation states that bones provide attachment points for muscles, but space permits recording one relation. Which compact statement preserves the supported relation?
op: Bones facilitate movement through muscle attachment points
Muscles facilitate movement through bone attachment points
Bones facilitate movement by storing minerals and fat
Bones facilitate movement by producing blood cells
mc.ex: Bones facilitate movement by providing attachment points for muscles. Reversing that relation incorrectly makes muscles the providers of attachment points for bones.

criticalDefects: Question 1 declares option 2 even though it reverses the source relation; option 0 is correct and the explanation supports option 0.
diagnoses.rationale: Both artifacts contain a critical first-question key error, but B is otherwise source-faithful, precise, scenario-ready, and well constructed. A additionally has unsupported clinical content, multiple correct alternatives, and unfinished feedback.

criticalDefects: The first question declares “Adult skeleton forms most hard, dense Bone,” but the supported answer is “System combines structures; Bone identifies connective tissue.”
The first explanation supports the system-versus-tissue alternative and therefore contradicts the declared answer.
diagnoses.rationale: Both artifacts contain a serious first-question key failure, but A otherwise stays faithful, supplies a strong decision scenario, and gives substantive feedback. B adds extensive unsupported clinical details, creates multiple supported alternatives, and leaves template text unfinished.
